originality.rationale: Full author preprint of Neininger (2001) analyzes comparison counts jointly with key-exchange counts, not input inversions; the Brodal-Fagerberg-Moruz (2004) report addresses adaptive costs against presortedness, not the independent joint limiting law; Iliopoulos (2015) is a survey with inversions appearing in a different sorting context; Baxter-Zeilberger (2010) gives inversion/major-index joint Gaussian behavior, not Quicksort/inversion. Exact zero covariance and univariate limits are explicitly prior or background. The new claim is a nonlinear decorrelation estimate and independent two-coordinate limit for exact objects. Residual risk remains implicit coverage by general functional limit theory or inaccessible full text.
residual_risks: An unlocated general theorem on stable asymptotics of random permutation statistics could imply the qualitative product limit.

value.rationale: The mathematically natural question is joint behavior of comparison complexity and inversion-defined input disorder. Exact uncorrelation does not ensure independence; the result proves an explicit uniform bound for nonlinear test transformations and an independent limit of two different fluctuation scales. It supplies joint statistical understanding beyond known marginal laws, not a routine finite table or arbitrary parameter slice.
